deferred_source_units.source_text: For this man knows better than everyone that he is sinning, when he crafts fragile vessels and carved images from earthy material.
deferred_source_units.reason: Romans 1:21-23 concerns people who knew God but exchanged His glory for images. Wisdom 15:13 gives the craftsman a particular superior awareness that he is sinning, while 15:11 says he did not know his Maker. The different knowledge claims are not flattened into one identical assertion, so this proposed counterpart remains unretained.

deferred_source_units.source_text: For the dreams that troubled them had announced this beforehand, so that they would not perish without knowing why they suffered.
deferred_source_units.reason: Matthew 27:19 reports Pilate's wife suffering in a dream and urging him to avoid the righteous Man. It does not announce the dreamer's own future death or explain why she would die, as Wisdom says its dreams explained impending suffering. The narrower forewarning-and-reason claim remains unsupported by this candidate.

target_units.text: because, although they knew God, they did not glorify Him as God or give thanks, but became futile in their thoughts, and their senseless heart was darkened.
Claiming to be wise, they became foolish,
and exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for the likeness of an image of corruptible humanity, and of birds and four-footed animals and creeping things.
